# Ludicord

> Ludicord is a full-stack React and TypeScript framework for building Discord
> Activities on the Discord Embedded App SDK. It provides file-system routing,
> Discord authentication, HTTP API routes, WebSockets, multiplayer rooms,
> shared state, typed navigation, compiler plugins, WebAssembly support, and
> production tooling.

Current stable documentation: Ludicord 4.1.1.

## Canonical links

- [Website](https://ludicord.extra.codes/)
- [Documentation](https://ludicord.extra.codes/docs)
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ludicord)
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/mrcholer/ludicord)
- [Community tutorials](https://github.com/mrcholer/ludicord/discussions/3)
- [Issues](https://github.com/mrcholer/ludicord/issues)

## Core conventions

- `app/page.tsx` defines a pathname page and Activity boundary scope.
- `app/**/embed.tsx` defines an Activity screen owned by its nearest page.
- `app/**/route.ts` defines an authenticated HTTP route.
- `app/**/socket.ts` defines an authenticated WebSocket route.
- `ludicord.config.mjs` owns Discord, Activity, server, WebSocket, import alias,
  and compiler-plugin configuration.
- `LudicordActivity` initializes Discord, authentication, shared event stores,
  safe-area values, and embed routing.
- Use `Link` or `useEmbedRouter()` inside one page and `PrefixLink` only when
  navigation must move to another justified pathname page.
- Keep secrets in server-only environment variables. Never trust browser-sent
  identity when `request.ludicord` or `client.ludicord` provides verified data.

## Quick start

```bash
npm create ludicord-app@latest my-activity
cd my-activity
npm run dev
```

Use the locally installed package as the authority. Check its declarations,
`ludicord.generated.d.ts`, `node_modules/ludicord/dist/docs/`, and
`node_modules/ludicord/dist/skills/ludicord/SKILL.md` before relying on public
examples from another version.
